title: Discovery: Reliability & fallbacks with Cobalt Finance
summary: Initial reliability discovery focusing on fallbacks, multi-region routing, and SLA expectations. Customer runs latency-sensitive payment flows and is evaluating Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private deployments for compliance and uptime. Key asks: multi-region failover, deterministic fallbacks to cheaper models, audit logs for incidents, and a pilot to validate SLOs.

transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-03-16 14:30 PDT
Duration: 42 minutes
Location: Zoom
Recording: yes
Attendees: Anna Lopez (Redwood AE), Marcus Chen (Redwood SE), Diego Ruiz (Redwood Solutions), Lina Patel (Head of Platform, Cobalt), Rajiv Kumar (SRE), Molly Chen (CISO), Ethan Brooks (PM)

Summary (auto): Quick discovery. Cobalt is evaluating Redwood for payment-authorization LLM workflows. Main concerns: incident tolerance, deterministic fallbacks during outages, multi-region failover, and compliance for PII. Wants clarity on SLA guarantees and what happens during partial region failures.

00:00 - 00:20 Anna Lopez: hey everyone thanks for joining really appreciate you carving time today um Marcus and I will run through a few reliability patterns and then we want to hear about your SLOs and constraints.
00:21 - 00:50 Lina Patel: thanks anna, quick context, we run payment auth rules + fraud heuristics, it's pretty latency sensitive sub-200ms target for the auth path, and we have a compliance window that requires logs retained for seven years, so on-prem or VPC is on the table if needed.
00:51 - 01:20 Marcus Chen: okay makes sense, so two buckets in terms of convo, 1) what our hosted product provides today for multi-region failover and automatic fallbacks, 2) what Dedicated/Private gives you for stricter isolation and on-prem routing, and 3) the actual policy examples and SLA behaviors.
01:21 - 02:00 Rajiv Kumar: curious about how fallbacks work in practice — like if your primary model cluster in us-west goes down, do we route to a smaller model in us-east automatically, and what about tokenization/state — we use prefix caching and KV cache so session continuity matters.
02:01 - 02:40 Marcus Chen: yep so we do prefix/KV caching yes — sometimes transcribed as "KV cash" — the runtime maintains cache hints and we support model pairs where keys can be translated, there's small possible cold-start gap if you flip regions but the cache design reduces repeat prefix compute. for fallbacks we support policy-based routing: cost-first, latency-first, and region-affinity.
02:41 - 03:10 Molly Chen: and for security, we need KMS integration and audit logs for any model calls, plus SAML for SSO — do you support customer-managed keys in hosted?
03:11 - 03:50 Anna Lopez: yes hosted supports customer KMS via our enterprise plan, you can bring your keys and logs are exported to your SIEM — we'll share the security pack but yes SOC2 and ISO attestations available.
03:51 - 04:30 Ethan Brooks: also can you do deterministic fallback policies — e.g., if high-quality large model fails we want to fallback to a smaller quantized model but only for a specific route and with a visible downgrade flag in the response so downstream knows quality changed.
04:31 - 05:00 Marcus Chen: good ask — we support per-route fallback chains with explicit downgrade metadata in the response header body so your services can detect degradation and apply mitigation. That metadata can include model id, quant profile, and reason code.
05:01 - 05:35 Lina Patel: latency vs cost is our constant tradeoff. our finance team will push lower-cost options but our product team needs consistency. what percent of time do you see region switches add to p50/p99?
05:36 - 06:20 Marcus Chen: region switch adds usually 50-200ms depending on model and sequence length — for short chat style inference you're often under 100ms p50, but cold-start p99 could spike. our platform has pre-warmed standby capability in Dedicated that limits that.
06:21 - 06:55 Rajiv Kumar: what about automatic fallback to cached replies — like can we cache certain prompts and serve from cache if the model is slow or down? and is that tenant-aware?
06:56 - 07:40 Anna Lopez: yes prefix and response caching is tenant-aware; you can configure TTLs and also a route-level policy to use cache-only for certain critical paths during incidents.
07:41 - 08:30 Marcus Chen: also we have rollout tools — canary, A/B, and automatic fallback policies — so you can test a smaller model and then automatically revert if latency or quality thresholds break.
08:31 - 09:10 Lina Patel: for Dedicated, what's the isolation story? we want predictable throughput and to avoid noisy neighbors during Black Friday like peaks.
09:11 - 09:50 Anna Lopez: Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools, you can configure autoscaling policies and reserved headroom for spikes; SLAs increase for Dedicated contracts — we'll attach the SLA table in the follow-up.
09:51 - 10:40 Molly Chen: SLA specifics — we need 99.95% availability for our auth path, and a clear incident timeline (notify within 15 minutes, RCA within 72 hours). do you commit to that?
10:41 - 11:20 Marcus Chen: our enterprise SLA for Dedicated can go up to 99.95% with an incident response playbook, 15 minute operational alerting is available with premium plan, RCA within 72 hours typically. we'll surface exact language in the contract.
11:21 - 12:00 Rajiv Kumar: multi-region routing — do you support active-active across regions or is it active-passive? we prefer active-active for lower latency but worry about consistency and state for long-lived sessions.
12:01 - 12:50 Marcus Chen: we support both. active-active requires sticky routing or cross-region KV replication; currently hosted prefers active-passive with automated failover but Dedicated/Private can be configured active-active with cross-region KV replication if you accept higher complexity.
12:51 - 13:30 Lina Patel: ok can you quantify failover times in both modes?
13:31 - 14:10 Marcus Chen: active-passive typical failover detection plus routing redistribution is ~30-90 seconds if health checks detect outage, plus any KV rehydration which can be minutes for large session state; active-active with replication reduces perceived failover to sub-second for routing but requires sync and is heavier on cost.
14:11 - 15:00 Ethan Brooks: curious about partial region degradation — if a subset of nodes in us-west have issues but not full region down, do you do granular routing at AZ level?
15:01 - 15:40 Marcus Chen: yes we have health checks per cluster and per-AZ; smart routing can avoid bad AZs within region and we can move traffic to other AZs or regions per policy.
15:41 - 16:20 Lina Patel: for our compliance we likely need Private with VPC peering, but the first step is a pilot — can that pilot be hosted with customer KMS and a dedicated pool?
16:21 - 17:00 Anna Lopez: yes many customers run pilots on hosted enterprise offering with customer-managed keys and logical dedicated pools; if pilot goes well we can transition to Dedicated or Private with minimal config changes.
17:01 - 17:40 Rajiv Kumar: request: want a fail-open vs fail-closed policy for auth routes — sometimes we want to fail-closed (deny) if model is unavailable, sometimes fail-open (pass to legacy rules) — can routing support that?
17:41 - 18:20 Marcus Chen: routing supports policy flags per-route: fail-open, fail-closed, degrade-to-cache, degrade-to-rule-engine. you can mix and match per endpoint.
18:21 - 19:00 Molly Chen: on the audit side, incident logs need to be immutable and time-series for at least seven years, legal wants tamper-evident storage — do you integrate with HSM backed KMS for that?
19:01 - 19:40 Anna Lopez: yes we support HSM-backed KMS integrations on Private and Dedicated plans; hosted enterprise supports customer KMS via cloud providers, and we can ship immutable logs to your long-term store as part of the compliance package.
19:41 - 20:20 Ethan Brooks: pricing question — in a failover scenario when traffic routes to more expensive region or larger model, is there a way to cap cost? we need cost controls for burst events.
20:21 - 21:00 Marcus Chen: yes you can set budget caps and automated routing policies that prefer cheaper region/model; if cap is hit you can either throttle or switch to cached/responder fallback. we also support billing alerts.
21:01 - 21:40 Lina Patel: timeline — we'd like a pilot in April to validate p50/p95 under our load. what would you need from us?
21:41 - 22:30 Anna Lopez: sample traffic traces, schema of requests, a list of routes you want to test, and your SLA targets; Marcus will send a benchmark template.
22:31 - 23:10 Rajiv Kumar: small nit: how do you handle encryption in transit between regions? we have strict internal regulations.
23:11 - 23:50 Marcus Chen: all inter-region traffic is TLS and we support mTLS for Dedicated/Private. we can provide cert rotation docs.
23:51 - 24:30 Lina Patel: any known gotchas with fallbacks and hallucination risks — our product team worries about quality drop when falling back to quantized models.
24:31 - 25:10 Marcus Chen: we recommend a graded fallback chain with safeguards: add a quality sentinel in the pipeline, monitor outputs with eval prompts and auto-rollback if QC drops. Redwood Optimize can suggest quant profiles per workload.
25:11 - 26:00 Molly Chen: do you provide per-tenant tracing so we can correlate incidents to customer request ids?
26:01 - 26:40 Anna Lopez: yes full tracing with trace IDs, request ids and token-level cost/latency breakdowns available in Console.
26:41 - 27:30 Ethan Brooks: good. final question: contractual remedies — do you offer service credits for SLA breaches and is it in the contract?
27:31 - 28:10 Anna Lopez: yes service credits for measured SLA breaches, we can share the SLA exhibit language.
28:11 - 28:50 Lina Patel: next steps recap?
28:51 - 29:40 Anna Lopez: we'll send pricing + dedicated comparison, security pack, benchmark template; Marcus to schedule deep-dive and runbook; propose pilot in early April.
29:41 - 30:20 Rajiv Kumar: I'll share traffic trace and list of critical routes by Thursday.
30:21 - 31:00 Marcus Chen: I'll include a sample routing policy and example JSON for fallback chains.
31:01 - 32:00 Molly Chen: can you also include legal redlines for KMS and data residency?
32:01 - 32:40 Anna Lopez: yes we'll loop legal in follow-up and attach the compliance exhibit.
32:41 - 34:00 Closing small talk, scheduling follow-up.

Note: transcription contains occasional misrecognitions ("KV cash" instead of KV cache, "VendorX" used as placeholder). Links mentioned: Security pack (https://app.redwood.example/security-pack/cobalt), Pricing sheet (https://app.redwood.example/pricing/dedicated-vs-hosted.pdf), Benchmark template (https://app.redwood.example/benchmarks/template.xlsx).

- SE to schedule 2-hour deep-dive and provide benchmark template (Marcus)
